contract: predict_distributions(regions) -> dict {region: {species_id: float array (n_sites,)}} of habitat-suitability scores (any finite real numbers; only their ranking matters) at the presence-absence survey sites of each species' biological group. regions maps AWT, CAN, NSW, NZ, SA and SWI to dicts with covariates (list of k names), categorical (names of categorical covariates: CAN ontveg, NSW vegsys, NZ age and toxicats, SWI calc), coordinates (text naming the x/y system), presence {species_id: {'x': (n, k) covariate values, 'xy': (n, 2) coordinates}} of presence-only records, background {'x': (m, k), 'xy': (m, 2)} of random background points, and sites {group: {'x': (s, k), 'xy': (s, 2), 'species': [ids of the species evaluated at these sites]}}; NaN marks a missing covariate value. Presence-absence outcomes at the sites are never provided. The candidate runs in a separate sandboxed process (numpy, scipy, scikit-learn and pandas importable; no file, network or subprocess access; one thread) with 300 s of CPU time for fitting and all predictions together; seed any randomness so that results are deterministic. Score: mean over the 226 species of the area under the ROC curve (tied scores count one half) of the site scores against the observed presences and absences; higher is better. Missing species, wrong shapes or non-finite scores are invalid
notes: Scores are recomputed from pinned public data prepared by scripts/prepare_earth.py; held-out data never enter the candidate's sandboxed process. The held-out observations are public, so a fixed candidate should be checked on later data before any scientific claim.
protocol_description: Locally implemented or adapted evaluator for the cited task or benchmark. Data sources, generated instances, evaluation budgets and protocol differences are specified in the candidate contract, requirements and notes; scores are not automatically comparable with published results.
name: Earth science: species distribution models from presence-only records
description: Fit species distribution models for 226 anonymised species in six regions from presence-only records, background points and environmental covariates, and score sites of independent presence-absence surveys whose outcomes are withheld. The score is the mean area under the ROC curve over species.
benchmark: Earth science: species distribution models from presence-only records
paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

sources.locator: Elith et al. (2006): comparison of species distribution modelling methods fitted to presence-only data and evaluated with independent presence-absence data in the same six regions.
Elith et al. (2020): description of the released benchmark data (226 species, presence-only training, background, presence-absence evaluation).
Valavi et al. (2022): benchmark of presence-only methods on these data with AUC as the main evaluation measure.
OSF project SDM_NCEAS (CC BY 4.0): train_po, train_bg, test_env and test_pa CSV files of the six regions; downloaded files match the SHA-256 hashes published by OSF.

limitations: AUC measures how well site scores rank surveyed presences above absences; it ignores calibration and prevalence, and survey absences include non-detections.
Site and record coordinates are provided, so spatial predictors are allowed; published comparisons mostly used environmental covariates only, so scores are not directly comparable with them.
No published value is embedded: the benchmark paper's tables could not be retrieved in this environment (the publisher's site refused the request), so the mean AUCs it reports were not checked.
The presence-absence outcomes are public on OSF; the sandbox keeps them away from the candidate process, but search feedback on these fixed sites can still overfit them.
A better score is a better species distribution modelling method on this benchmark, not an ecological discovery.

The candidate runs in a sandboxed child process that never receives the survey outcomes, and no statement of the candidate is executed in the evaluator's process; outside macOS (kernel sandbox) deliberately hostile native code could bypass the file policy.

state_of_the_art.statement: No published value is embedded (see limitations). The seed, a per-covariate Gaussian presence/background density ratio without categorical covariates, scores a mean AUC of 0.709 (region means 0.48 for CAN to 0.78 for SA).

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict where a species occurs from presence-only occurrence records and environmental covariates (species distribution modelling).
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Species distribution models are the main tool for mapping biodiversity, planning conservation and projecting climate-change impacts on species; presence-only records are the commonest data, and how well methods predict independent surveys is a central methodological question in ecology.

papers.title: Novel methods improve prediction of species' distributions from occurrence data
papers.primary_goal: Compare the predictive performance of species distribution modelling methods fitted to presence-only data, using independent presence-absence data from six regions.
papers.task_relation: The task uses the released version of the same benchmark (226 species, six regions) and the same kind of evaluation (AUC on independent presence-absence sites).

papers.task_relation: Same data and AUC evaluation; the task lets any method be evolved and allows coordinates as predictors.
